text: The LORD said to Moses:
"Make yourself two trumpets of silver; make them of hammered work. You shall use them to summon the congregation and to set the camps in motion.
When both are blown, the whole congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, shall gather to you.
When you sound a blast, the camps on the east side shall set out.
When you sound a second blast, the camps on the south side shall set out. A blast is to be sounded whenever they are to march.
But when you call the assembly together, you shall blow a steady note, not a blast.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, are the ones to blow the trumpets. This shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who oppresses you, sound a blast on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.

On your days of gladness, at your appointed festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings. They will be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the testimony.
Then the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, stage by stage, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
This was the first time they set out at the command of the LORD through Moses.
The standard of the camp of Judah went first, company by company, and Nahshon son of Amminadab was over its company.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the company of the tribe of Issachar,
and Eliab son of Helon was over the company of the tribe of Zebulun.
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites, who carried it, set out.
Next the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, company by company, and Elizur son of Shedeur was over its company.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the company of the tribe of Simeon,
and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the company of the tribe of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived.

versions.text: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things; the tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew states that the others (the Gershonites and Merarites) had erected the tabernacle by the time the Kohathites arrived. The modal 'was to be set up' introduces a sense of obligation not in the text, and the semicolon breaks the oral flow; a simple past passive reads more naturally and stays closer to the sense.

text: Next the standard of the camp of Ephraim set out, company by company, and Elishama son of Ammihud was over its company.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the company of the tribe of Manasseh,
and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the company of the tribe of Benjamin.
Finally the standard of the camp of Dan set out as rear guard for all the camps, company by company, and Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over its company.
Pagiel son of Ochran was over the company of the tribe of Asher,
and Ahira son of Enan was over the company of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the marching order of the Israelites, company by company, as they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."

versions.text: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, his father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
versions.explanation: 'His father-in-law' is ambiguous in English (whose father-in-law?), while the Hebrew explicitly names Moses. Naming Moses removes the ambiguity for a listener, though the phrase may still describe either Hobab or Reuel; a footnote noting this ambiguity would add value.

text: But he answered, "I will not go. I am going back to my own land and my own people."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good the LORD gives us."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and traveled for three days, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them those three days to seek out a resting place for them.
And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day whenever they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, "Rise up, O LORD! Let your enemies be scattered; let those who hate you flee before you."
And whenever it came to rest, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."
